Theme

School & learning

plural noun

in grammar

also plural number, in the plural, plurals, singular and plural

classical

Quint. 1.5.42: in quibus nōs singulārem ac plūrālem habēmus
Quint. 1.6.26 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 221, 248

plūrālis, plūrāle

declension

plural, of more than one

numerus plūrālis, the plural number; adverb plūrāliter, in the plural (Sen. NQ 2.56.1; Quint. 1.6.25). Traupman also gives multitūdō for “a plural”, from his pupil’s multitūdinem significāns, meaning a plural (248, 221).

Other words

  • numerus plūrālis

    also used · classical · Quint. 1.5.42: numerōs, in quibus nōs singulārem ac plūrālem habēmus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 361

    The number as a whole, in Quintilian; “in the plural” is plūrāliter.

  • multitūdō, multitūdinis f. — the plural (number)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Varr. LL 9.63 (Lewis & Short s.v. multitūdō); Gell. 19.8.13: numerum multitūdinis capiunt (Lewis & Short); Traupman 361

    The older grammatical term, numerus multitūdinis, or simply multitūdō.

Examples

  • tonitrua nōs plūrāliter dīcimus

    we say tonitrua in the pluralSen. NQ 2.56.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • Dīc plūrālem prīmae persōnae.

    Give the first person plural.Traupman 241

  • plūrāliter

    in the pluralTraupman 361

  • multitūdinem significāns

    signifying a pluralTraupman 361
